chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Rank the hydrogen halides in order of increasing Brønsted acidity (lowest to highest):
questions.explanation: Down the halogen group, larger orbital size and weaker H-X bond strength dominate over electronegativity, increasing acidity.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Rank the following four-carbon compounds in order of increasing boiling point:

options.label: C
options.text: n-Butane (-0.5°C, London dispersion) < Diethyl ether (34.5°C, dipole-dipole) < 1-Butanol (117°C, H-bonding) < Butanoic acid (164°C, H-bonded dimer).

questions.correct_answer: n-Butane (-0.5°C, London dispersion) < Diethyl ether (34.5°C, dipole-dipole) < 1-Butanol (117°C, H-bonding) < Butanoic acid (164°C, H-bonded dimer).
questions.explanation: Boiling point increases with the strength of intermolecular forces: London dispersion < dipole-dipole < single H-bonding < dual H-bonded dimerization.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Rank the following carbon-heteroatom single bonds in order of increasing bond dipole moment (lowest to highest):
questions.explanation: Dipole moment increases directly with the electronegativity difference (ΔEN) across the carbon-heteroatom bond.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Rank the three C₅H₁₂ pentane isomers in order of increasing boiling point:

options.label: B
options.text: All three isomers have identical boiling points.

questions.explanation: Spherical branched isomers have lower surface contact area and weaker London dispersion forces, lowering boiling points.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Rank the following carbonyl compounds in order of increasing equilibrium constant for hydration (K_hyd in water):

options.label: A
options.text: All three carbonyls have identical K_hyd.

questions.explanation: Electron-donating alkyl groups and steric crowding stabilize the carbonyl group, reducing hydration equilibrium from formaldehyde to acetone.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Water vs Alcohol vs Alkyne Acidity Ranking
questions.question: Rank the following Brønsted acids in order of increasing acidity (lowest to highest):

options.label: A
options.text: Water < Ethanol < Acetic acid < Acetylene < Ethane.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethane (pKa 50) < Acetylene (pKa 25) < Ethanol (pKa 16) < Water (pKa 15.7) < Acetic acid (pKa 4.76).

options.label: C
options.text: Ethane < Ethanol < Acetylene < Water < Acetic acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Acetic acid < Water < Ethanol < Acetylene < Ethane.

questions.correct_answer: Ethane (pKa 50) < Acetylene (pKa 25) < Ethanol (pKa 16) < Water (pKa 15.7) < Acetic acid (pKa 4.76).
questions.explanation: Acidity increases according to ARIO rules: sp³ C-H < sp C-H < O-H (alcohol) < O-H (water) < resonance-stabilized carboxyl O-H.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Ammonia vs Water vs Methane Basicity Ranking
questions.question: Rank the conjugate bases in order of increasing basicity (weakest to strongest base):

options.label: A
options.text: Hydroxide ion (OH⁻) < Amide ion (NH₂⁻) < Methanide carbanion (CH₃⁻).

questions.correct_answer: Hydroxide ion (OH⁻) < Amide ion (NH₂⁻) < Methanide carbanion (CH₃⁻).
questions.explanation: Across a row in the periodic table, electronegativity increases (C < N < O), stabilizing negative charge and decreasing basicity.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Lewis Acidity Ranking of Boron Trihalides
questions.question: Rank the boron trihalides in order of increasing Lewis acidity toward pyridine:

options.label: B
options.text: All boron trihalides have identical Lewis acidity.

questions.explanation: Planar (p-p)π backbonding is strongest in BF₃ (matching 2p orbitals), reducing the electrophilicity of boron compared to larger halides.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Rank the following halomethanes in order of increasing molecular dipole moment:

options.label: A
options.text: CCl₄ (0 D) < CHCl₃ (1.04 D) < CH₂Cl₂ (1.60 D) < CH₃Cl (1.87 D).

options.label: B
options.text: Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄, μ = 0 D) < Methyl chloride (CH₃Cl, 1.87 D) < Dichloromethane (CH₂Cl₂, 1.60 D) < Chloroform (CHCl₃, 1.04 D).

questions.correct_answer: Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄, μ = 0 D) < Methyl chloride (CH₃Cl, 1.87 D) < Dichloromethane (CH₂Cl₂, 1.60 D) < Chloroform (CHCl₃, 1.04 D).
questions.explanation: Symmetric tetrahedral CCl₄ cancels dipoles completely (0 D); CH₃Cl has the maximal uncompensated vector sum (1.87 D).

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Solvation Free Energy of Alkali Metal Cations
questions.question: Rank the alkali metal cations in order of increasing enthalpy of hydration (most negative ΔH_hyd):

options.label: A
options.text: All alkali cations have identical hydration energy.

questions.explanation: Smaller ionic radius increases charge density (q/r), maximizing ion-dipole electrostatic interaction with water molecules.

options.text: All boron trihalides have identical Lewis acidity.

questions.explanation: Planar (p-p)π backbonding is strongest in BF₃ (matching 2p orbitals), reducing the electrophilicity of boron compared to larger halides.

boss_strategy.progression: Easy questions decrease by 1 per boss, Medium questions remain at 4, Hard questions increase by 1 per boss.
